clue.text: Blue language?

parts.note: ... Blue is a well-known blue cheese, so the tongue of Denmark is the language that comes before Blue

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a term for swearing or smutty talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue language' normally means obscene talk; here the language is the one whose name precedes 'Blue' in a famous Danish cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic: the national language of Denmark shares its name with Danish Blue cheese.

clue.text: Assist young dog to get a trim on top

indicators.text: to get a trim on top
indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and trimming it removes that letter

parts.note: a whelp is a puppy or young dog

explanation.surface: Instructions to help a puppy by clipping its head fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get a trim on top' cuts the first letter, W, from WHELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to assist someone is to aid or support them.

clue.text: Crazy person taking one drug after another

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
a second drug: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A madman who takes drugs one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a crank or eccentric with mad ideas is called this.

clue.text: Fine-tune commercial objective

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
objective in the sense of impartial, fair, just

explanation.surface: Tweaking an advert's goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objective' reads as a noun (a goal) but works as the adjective meaning impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fine-tune something is to make small corrective changes to it.

clue.text: Church high-up's cold, seeking accommodation in parish with hob for cooking

indicators.note: looking to be housed within, so the cold letter goes inside the other letters
cooking suggests ingredients mixed up, so the letters of parish and hob are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A senior cleric with a chill looks for lodgings in a parish, with a hob to cook on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' makes the letters ARHBISHOP; 'seeking accommodation in' houses the cold letter inside them. The 's after the definition stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop is among the most senior figures in a church hierarchy, a true church high-up.

clue.text: Salary cap — one's on the bottle!

parts.note: screw is old British slang for wages or salary
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: A limit on pay drives someone to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREW is dated British slang for a wage. 'Salary cap' looks like a pay limit; 'on the bottle' looks like heavy drinking, but the definition is literal: this lid sits on a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid with a thread twisted onto a bottle neck is this kind of closure.

clue.text: Accept members ready to fight

definitions.note: ready as a verb: to prepare oneself for fighting

parts.note: to accept something is to take it
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Taking on new members who are keen for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take up weapons is to get oneself ready for fighting.

clue.text: I start getting troubles, being easy victim

indicators.note: troubles as a verb, stirring up or disturbing these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that trouble keeps finding them, as if they were a soft touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' rearranges the thirteen letters of I START GETTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something stationary that cannot dodge is easily hit, so a defenceless person is one.

clue.text: Frank's awful heartless cat

parts.note: dire means dreadful or awful

indicators.note: without its heart, so the central letter of cat goes

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank owns a dreadful, cruel cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid; 's is 'is'. 'heartless' drops A from CAT, leaving CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frank speech is straightforward and to the point.

clue.text: Independent work I found in British Columbia making film

indicators.note: located within, so the inner letters sit inside the abbreviation

parts.note: BC is the abbreviation for the Canadian province
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An independent production shot in British Columbia becomes a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film, a movie about a real person's life.

clue.text: Clumsily I cut hero, more likely to act hurt

indicators.note: done clumsily, the letters of I, cut and hero are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who accidentally wounded a hero, who is now sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of touchy: a more sensitive person takes offence more readily.

clue.text: Examination site where those with correct papers may pass

definitions.text: where those with correct papers may pass

parts.note: a check is an inspection or examination
a point is a place or site

explanation.surface: Describes a border post where documents are inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier where guards inspect documents lets through only travellers whose paperwork is in order.

clue.text: Study on Southern crime in the main produces intrigue

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the main is the open sea, and robbery at sea is piracy

explanation.surface: A report on a major southern crime reveals a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: intrigue as a noun is a secret plot, a scheme hatched by plotters.

clue.text: Greek character's ten cheers

parts.note: 10 written as the letters I and O
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A Greek gives ten rousing cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. TA and 'cheers' are both everyday British ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character in that script.

clue.text: Enforce efficiency as captain with a drunken crew?

definitions.meaning: to manage something with strict discipline and order
tight is slang for drunk, so a vessel full of tipsy sailors is literally a tight ship to command

explanation.surface: A skipper keeps order despite his sailors being drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for strict management, and literally commanding a vessel whose sailors are tight, meaning drunk.

clue.text: Farmer hurried around, brave fellow

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to hurry
C stands for circa, Latin for around or about
a hero is a brave man

explanation.surface: A farmer rushed about like some bold champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a rancher in Mexico or the US southwest, someone farming livestock.

clue.text: Experimental piece of glassware?

parts.note: seems to mean a prototype glass object, but describes the narrow glass vessel used in lab experiments

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a trial design by a glassmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow glass cylinder closed at one end, used for holding samples in laboratory experiments.

clue.text: Bargain crop

definitions.meaning: British informal: something cheap, a real bargain
to crop is to cut or clip, as with scissors

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: British slang for a cheap purchase, and the verb meaning to cut with scissors.

clue.text: Engineer appeals about barrier, wobbly thing in pipe below head

definitions.text: wobbly thing in pipe below head

indicators.note: placed around, so the rearranged letters surround the barrier
as a verb, to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters of appeals are rearranged

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river

explanation.surface: An engineer petitions over a dam, while a plumber's pipe wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' makes the letters ASAPPLE, and 'about' wraps them round the barrier. The 'pipe' is the windpipe, not a plumber's, and 'head' is the human head.
explanation.definitionFit: The lump of laryngeal cartilage in the throat bobs when you swallow; the throat is a pipe beneath the head.

clue.text: Birds roost here through sitting under a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting under another comes after it

parts.note: via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Birds perch on a railway, under a bridge perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'sitting under' means coming below, that is after, the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure where birds are kept, so they roost there.

clue.text: Congestion record spread

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
jam is a fruit spread for bread

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a report on the spread of traffic jams.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle of floating timber blocking a river, and so any blockage or standstill.

clue.text: Prince in story's chapter causing damage

parts.note: harming means doing damage

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale prince has a chapter where he wreaks havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero who marries Cinderella in the fairy tale is named Prince Charming.

clue.text: That man should avoid the rough depression

indicators.note: avoiding these letters means leaving them out of the phrase

parts.note: he means that man

explanation.surface: Golf advice: a player ought to keep out of the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rough' is golf's long grass beside the fairway. 'should avoid' takes HE out of THE ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a low point or hollow, as in a weather chart's low-pressure dip.

clue.text: Bess's partner lacking power in party

indicators.note: without, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: Porgy is Bess's partner in Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Bess's partner lacks energy at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, unrestrained party.

clue.text: More vulgar-sounding shopkeeper

indicators.note: sounding like signals a word spoken that matches another

parts.note: grosser means coarser or more vulgar

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper with an even coarser tone of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a trader who sells food and household goods from a store.

clue.text: Vehicle to bring back horse beyond marsh

indicators.note: placed past, so the horse comes after the marsh

parts.note: a bog is a marsh

indicators.note: bringing back means the word for horse is read in reverse

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Instructions to lead a horse back across a marsh in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring back' makes GAN of the horse; 'beyond' puts it after the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a long sled, a vehicle for sliding down snowy slopes.
